Its finding was independently re-verified before any change: read both real, current call sites (runtime/src/normalize/mod.rs's normalize_typed_obligations and the identical inline logic in runtime/src/census/mod.rs's build_census) directly, then hand-traced Rust's actual Vec::dedup_by semantics (it only ever compares an element to the immediately preceding one it KEPT, never a full pairwise scan within a sort-key group) to confirm the claimed mechanism was real, not merely plausible-sounding. key_finding: Both normalize_typed_obligations (runtime/src/normalize/mod.rs) and the identical inline dedup logic inside build_census (runtime/src/census/mod.rs) sorted a Vec<SemanticObligationRecord> by obligation_id alone, then called dedup_by(|a, b| a == b) -- a full-struct-equality comparator strictly finer than the sort key. Vec::dedup_by only ever compares an element to the immediately preceding element it decided to keep, never performing a full pairwise scan within a group of sort-key-equal elements. When the module's own documented 'same obligation_id always carries identical content' invariant is violated -- exactly the multi-census-run-merge scenario this normalization step exists to handle -- and a third, content-differing record happens to sit between two byte-identical ones in the ORIGINAL input order, a stable sort on the coarser key alone does not force the equal pair adjacent, so dedup_by silently fails to collapse them. The same logical multiset of three obligations (two identical, one different) therefore deduplicates to either 2 or 3 records purely depending on incidental input order -- a real nondeterminism bug, not merely a display/cosmetic issue, since typed_obligations feeds NormalizationReport.typed_obligations_total and the typed_obligations vector itself, both canonical, evidence-bearing parts of the census/normalization report.
verification_before_acting: Read both real, current call sites directly (not from the subagent's paraphrase) to confirm the exact sort_by/dedup_by code shape at each of the two locations.

Hand-traced Rust's actual Vec::dedup_by algorithm (compares only to the immediately preceding KEPT element, never a full pairwise scan) rather than trusting the subagent's description of std library behavior -- confirmed this matches the documented behavior of dedup_by ('Removes all but the first of consecutive elements... satisfying a given equality relation').

Confirmed SemanticObligationRecord derives both PartialEq/Eq and Debug (#[derive(Debug, Clone, Serialize, Deserialize, PartialEq, Eq)] in core/src/semantic/obligation.rs) with no custom Debug impl anywhere in the core crate (grepped for `impl.*Debug for`, found none) -- establishing that a Debug-string secondary sort key is provably as fine as the PartialEq comparator for this specific type (derived Debug prints every field in declaration order; derived PartialEq compares every field; two records differ in content iff they differ in at least one field iff their derived Debug strings differ).

Confirmed the sibling function normalize_typed_records (same file) already avoids this exact trap by including the dedup key (raw_observation_id) directly in its sort key -- establishing this fix follows an already-proven-correct pattern already present in this same file, not a novel approach.

Independently constructed the 3-element sandwich scenario and confirmed it reproduces against the real, unfixed code (both via a standalone unit test on normalize_typed_obligations and, separately, via a full build_census integration test through real ExtractionBatch inputs) before writing the fix -- not merely trusting the subagent's claimed terminal output.

design_decisions.question: How to make the sort key as fine as the dedup_by equality comparator, without a larger, riskier change (e.g. deriving Ord on SemanticObligationRecord and every field type it transitively contains)?
design_decisions.decision: Tie-break the existing obligation_id-based sort on the full derived Debug representation (format!("{a:?}")) rather than deriving PartialOrd/Ord on SemanticObligationRecord. Several of its field types (RevisionRef, EpistemicStatus) derive only PartialEq/Eq, not PartialOrd/Ord, in shared modules used throughout the codebase -- adding Ord derives there would be a much larger, riskier ripple than this narrow fix warrants. The Debug-string tie-break is fully self-contained to these two call sites, requires no changes to any shared type, and is provably correct for this specific type given its derived (never custom) Debug/PartialEq impls.

design_decisions.question: Fix only one of the two call sites, or both?
design_decisions.decision: Both -- this is byte-for-byte duplicated logic (not shared via a common function) in two independent files, and fixing only one would leave the sibling with the identical latent bug, exactly the kind of drift this session's own prior generations (e.g. is_panic_like_macro's unification) have explicitly called out as a real risk in this codebase.
